candidates.changed_node: denominator TS_MAX($high, 21) - TS_MIN($low, 21) -> TS_MEAN($high - $low, 21), with the numerator's adjusted $close swapped to raw $high to keep one price scale
candidates.rationale: Weakest component: the denominator TS_MAX($high,21) - TS_MIN($low,21). It bounds the factor in [0,1] using the same two extremes as the numerator, so the statistic saturates and its IC decays monotonically to nothing (2000 +0.0250 -> 2012 +0.0027 -> 2013 +0.0010). Replacing it with the 21d average daily range turns the same distance-from-the-low into an unbounded, volatility-normalized distance that keeps separating names when the range is wide. The numerator leaf moves $close -> $high in the same edit because $close is adjusted while TS_MIN($low,21) is raw, and that difference was a units error importing dividend information. Both terms are now raw OHLC, only TS_MIN($low,21) (3 nodes) survives from the parent, and coverage is unchanged at a 21d window.

Weakest component: the raw $volume level as the first correlation input. A level correlated against range picks up slow co-drift in liquidity and size, which is why the sign flips in the two calm, low-dispersion years (2003 -0.0051, 2013 -0.0013) and why mean IC is only 0.00703. Differencing volume by one day makes the correlation measure whether volume surprises land on wide bars rather than whether both series trend together, which is the stress/illiquidity effect the factor is meant to capture. Working memory 6 says volume paid only against a second series, so the correlation shape is kept; only its input changes. Shared structure with the parent drops to $high - $low (3 nodes).

candidates.changed_node: fundamental leaf $roe -> $operating_margin (range-leg windows 10 -> 21 to clear the near-copy gate)
candidates.rationale: Weakest component: the $roe leaf. It is what pins |rho| at 0.710 against the archive's RANK($roa) - the two are near-mechanical restatements of profitability - and the correlation gate, not the fitness, is this factor's binding constraint. $operating_margin is the margin leg of the same decomposition, carries the pricing-power part of quality without the leverage and asset-base terms that make roe track roa, and leaves the winning shape (demeaned fundamental rank times price-normalized range, working memory 5) intact. CS_DEMEAN is kept deliberately: it is what gives the product its long-short direction rather than a non-negative magnitude. The two windows move 10 -> 21 so no complete subtree of 4+ nodes carries over from the parent.

Weakest component: the second RANK's argument, ($open - TS_MIN($low,21)) / TS_MEAN($high,21). A within-range position is a fast, path-dependent statistic: it drives the highest turnover in the fundamental group (0.134 one-way), a 17.6-day half-life, and the two negative years (2003 -0.0086, 2012 -0.0012) where the range position inverts against the quality leg. Replacing it with relative price dispersion, TS_STD($high,21) normalized by the raw $open, keeps the same subtractive gate on the $roa rank but makes the price leg a smooth low-volatility tilt that reprices gradually. Turnover and the regime flips should both fall; only RANK($roa) (2 nodes) is retained from the parent.

Weakest component: the denominator TS_MAX($high, 21). It makes the price leg a ratio of two windows of one series, the construction that failed the cheap screen every time it was tried (working memory 8), and it compresses the leg into a narrow near-1 band that contributes little dispersion - the factor's t is the lowest of the quality-times-price group at 4.52 despite the best mean IC. Dividing the mean high by the parallel mean low instead compares two different series at the same window, giving the average relative range: a clean raw-scale volatility gate on the $roa rank rather than a drawdown proxy. Depth, fields and the multiplicative shape are unchanged, and only TS_MEAN($high, 21) (3 nodes) carries over.

candidates.changed_node: CS_RANK($roa) -> CS_RANK($asset_turnover) in the fundamental spread (gate numerator TS_MEAN($high, 21) -> TS_STD($high - $low, 21) to clear the near-copy gate)
candidates.rationale: Weakest component: the CS_RANK($roa) leg of the fundamental spread. It dominates the spread (working memory 10: that same spread hits rho 0.802 against RANK($roa) alone), holds this factor at |rho| 0.737 against the archive, and buys the weakest mean IC in the group, 0.00935. $asset_turnover is the other half of the same profitability decomposition, so the accrual gate still reads as quality-minus-earnings-manipulation, but the exposure is efficiency rather than a third copy of $roa. The gate numerator moves from a price level to the dispersion of the intraday range at the same 21d window and the same raw $open normalizer, both so no 4-plus-node subtree of the parent survives and because a level ratio is what turns negative in the trending year (2006 -0.0040).

candidates.changed_node: price leg $close / (TS_MAX($high, 189) + 1e-8) -> $open / (TS_MIN($low, 21) + 1e-8), with the vol window 126 -> 21
candidates.rationale: Weakest component: the price leg $close / (TS_MAX($high, 189) + 1e-8). It divides adjusted $close by raw $high, a scale error that imports future dividend information whatever fitness it reports, and its 189-day window plus the 126-day vol leg is what leaves coverage at 0.904, one point above the reject line. Recasting it as raw $open over the 21-day low extreme keeps the same idea - where the price sits inside its recent range - on one price scale and at a horizon that matches the 19.7-day IC half-life. The vol leg shortens to 21 in the same edit so the whole factor needs only 21 bars of history: coverage should go from 0.904 to roughly 0.99, and the fade to 2013 -0.0045 from stale long windows is removed.

Weakest component: the bare $volume leaf itself. As a level it is a size characteristic, not a signal - the IC never halves inside the 63-day grid, it still pays 0.153 one-way turnover, and it sits at |rho| 0.717 against the archive's dollar-volume mean, which is the same size exposure by another name. Working memory 6 says volume paid only when correlated against a second series, so the leaf is wrapped into a 21-day correlation with the raw high. That is size-free by construction (a correlation coefficient is scale-invariant), gives the factor a definite horizon, and measures flow-versus-price co-movement rather than how large the company is. It stays clear of the archive's volume-versus-range correlation, which uses a different second series.

Weakest component: the $roa leaf as a level. The level is already in the archive three times over (|rho| 0.737 against the gated version) and it is a slow-moving characteristic, 43-day half-life at 0.007 turnover, so it carries almost no information the archive does not already hold. Taking the quarterly change instead prices the improvement in profitability rather than its standing, which is close to orthogonal to the level cross-sectionally and should not repeat the archive's exposure. The window is 63 rather than the usual 21 because fundamentals are stamped quarterly: at 21 bars roughly two thirds of the panel would show an exact zero and the rank would be all ties. This is the one place the 21-bar rule has to give.

candidates.changed_node: momentum span DELAY($close, 21) / (DELAY($close, 147) + 1e-8) -> $close / (DELAY($close, 21) + 1e-8), with the vol window 105 -> 21
candidates.rationale: Weakest component: the momentum span DELAY($close, 21) / DELAY($close, 147). The IC half-life is 3.1 days, so essentially all the predictive content is in recent price action, yet the numerator deliberately discards the last 21 days and measures a seven-month move: the factor is built at a horizon its own content does not support, which is why 2009 goes to -0.0106 when the long span still holds the crash. Collapsing it to the 21-day return measured to the current close matches the construction to the 3-day decay and keeps the vol-normalized shape that earns the t. The vol window drops 105 -> 21 in the same edit, which lifts the maximum lookback to 21 bars and should raise coverage from 0.925, and it leaves no complete 4-plus-node subtree of the parent.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Keep lookbacks at 21 bars or fewer. Accepted expressions used only 2 and 21 bar windows; 42, 63, 126, and 189 bar lookbacks appeared exclusively in rejected proposals.
  2. Drop conditional regime splits. The single IF_ELSE proposal, switching between short-horizon reversal and momentum on high-low versus its 21d mean, had the worst cheap screen of the round at 0.48.
  3. RANK($roa) is too small to serve as a crossover parent. Both children built around it kept almost none of it while adding long-window volatility and price-extreme terms. Graft it whole as one operand of a larger donor expression, or cross from a bigger parent subtree instead.
  4. Normalize intraday-range terms by a raw OHLC field, as the accepted ones do with $open and ($high - $low). Do not divide OHLC quantities by $close: $close is adjusted while OHLC is raw, so mixing the scales is a units error that imports future dividend information.
  5. Multiplying a cross-sectional fundamental rank by a price-normalized range term is what paid: all three accepts above 4.0 had that shape. Every additive fundamental +/- volume-rank combo died on the cheap screen (|t| 0.52 and 0.06).
  6. Volume on its own is weak or duplicative: TS_ARGMAX($volume,21) scored 0.70, the 21d volume CV 1.43, and TS_RANK($volume,21) hit rho 0.94 against the dollar-volume z-score. Volume paid only when correlated against a second series (TS_CORR($volume, $high-$low, 21) = 4.98).
  7. $return as an input is dead on this fit window: TS_MEAN($return,21) gave |t| 0.35 and TS_CORR($return,$volume,10) gave |t| 0.09. Build the same ideas from price levels and $high-$low instead.
  8. Ratios of two windows of the same series failed the cheap screen every time (volume 5/21 -> 0.66, range 21/5 -> 0.19). Normalize against a different series or a price level, not against a longer window of itself.
  9. Near-copies of archive members caused 11 of 20 rejects: swapping one price leaf ($high for $close), one window constant (10->21, 21->189), inverting a ratio, or wrapping an existing term in TS_MEAN at the same window (rho 0.824). Change an operator or a whole input, not a parameter.
  10. A difference of two fundamental ranks submitted alone tracks its dominant leg (RANK($roa)-RANK($accrual_gap) hit rho 0.802 against RANK($roa)). The same spread cleared at 4.11 once multiplied by a price term, so gate fundamental spreads rather than proposing them bare.
  11. Do not put adjusted $close and raw OHLC in the same ratio or difference; it is a scale error that leaks future dividend information, whatever fitness it reports.
  12. Slot economics: fast/price_volume is held at only 1.43 and slow/price_volume at 0.70, so those are the cheap wins. slow/mixed is now held at 4.76 and 4.11 by fundamental-times-range factors, so further variants of that shape will mostly trip the correlation and subtree gates.
